title: Mwaro lycée teachers strike demanding systematic COVID testing
organizer: Teachers of the lycée de Mwaro; named organization unknown
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Over 80 COVID-positive pupils is not protest attendance. Public assembly and >=50 participating people not established.

title.summary: Reports a teachers strike over COVID testing.

start_date.summary: Bulletin situates begun strike in January; exact day absent.

demands.summary: Systematic tests for all pupils and personnel requested; labor workplace-health category tentative.

participants_original.summary: No striking-teacher attendance number; 80 concerns infected students.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No public assembly or attendance established.

state_response.summary: Communal education director and SNR chief reportedly appeared and threatened teachers over attempted January 26 suspension. No physical protest crowd or classified response proven; all seven coded responses unknown.

episode_unit.summary: Earlier generic Mwaro lycée strike and January 26 Mwaro II attempt may be one episode or different schools/actions. Boundary unresolved; no automatic merge or split into official observations.

notes: RPA media monitoring bulletin dated 19 January, published 20 January, reports teachers began a strike requesting systematic testing for all students and staff after pupil infections. No exact commencement day inferred. A work stoppage alone does not demonstrate a MM public gathering or domestic government target; labor category tentative for workplace-health demand. FORSC separately describes attempted suspension at Lycée Technique Communal Mwaro II January 26 and officials threatening teachers. Same school/episode relationship to generic lycée de Mwaro is unverified; retained as related evidence, no automatic new observation.
open_questions: Did teachers gather publicly and were at least 50 people present?
What exact date did the action start, and when did it physically end?
Which state institution or policy was the demand directed at?
Are the RPA lycée de Mwaro and FORSC Lycée Technique Communal Mwaro II the same establishment, and was January 26 a continuation or distinct attempt?

title: Ndava restaurant operators suspend business against daily municipal tax
organizer: Restaurant operators at Ndava commune center
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown; neither attendance nor public gathering is described.

title.summary: Restaurant operators suspended activities in tax dispute.

start_date.summary: Report explicitly dates suspension from January 11, 2021.

demands.summary: End daily 500 FBU commune levy; state municipal target explicit.

end_date.summary: No physical ending or suspension ending reported.

notes: FORSC reports suspension of restaurant activities starting January 11 against daily 500 FBU municipal levy added to annual 10000 FBU tax. Own-country municipal government target is explicit. Physical public assembly and >=50 persons are unproven; shop closures alone do not establish MM protest.
open_questions: Was there a public gathering of at least 50 people?
When did the suspension end and did it continue into February?
